en: Udāna 3.9 Sippasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion, after the meal, on returning from their alms round, a number of bhikkhus were sitting gathered together in the assembly hall when this discussion arose among them:
“Friends, who knows a craft?”
"Who has learned what craft?
Which craft is the foremost among crafts?
Thereupon, some spoke thus:
“Elephant-riding is the foremost of crafts,” some said. Others said,
“Horse-riding is the foremost of crafts.”
Some said this:
"The craft of charioteering is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
“The art of archery is the foremost of arts.
Some said thus:
“The art of swordsmanship is the foremost of arts.”
Some said this:
"The craft of calculation is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
“Arithmetic is the foremost of crafts,” some said. Others said:
“Accounting is the foremost of crafts.”
Some said this:
"The craft of writing is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
“Poetry is the foremost of crafts,” some say; others say,
“The Lokāyata craft is the foremost of crafts.”
Some said this:
"The science of the Khattavijas is the foremost of crafts.
Now, this discussion among those bhikkhus remained unfinished.
Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and went to the pavilion. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Sitting there, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
“Bhikkhus, for what discussion are you gathered here now, and what was the conversation of yours that was left unfinished?”
“Here, venerable sir, after we had returned from our almsround following the meal, we were sitting together in the assembly hall when this discussion arose among us:
‘Friends, who knows what craft?
Who has trained in what craft?’”
"Which craft is the foremost among crafts?
On this point, some said:
"The craft of elephant-riding is the foremost among crafts."
Some said this:
“The art of horse-riding is the foremost of arts.
Others said this:
‘The art of chariotry is the foremost of arts,’ some said. Others said,
‘The art of archery is the foremost of arts.’
Some said this:
“The craft of the sword is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
‘The art of sealing is the foremost of arts,’ some say;
‘the art of calculation is the foremost of arts,’ others say.
Some said this:
"The craft of calculation is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
‘The craft of writing is the foremost of crafts,’ some said. Others said:
‘The craft of poetry is the foremost of crafts.’
Some said this:
"The craft of Lokāyata is the foremost of crafts.
Others said this:
“‘The science of the Khattavijjā is the foremost of crafts,’ this was our conversation,
Bhante, which remained unfinished when the Blessed One arrived.
“Bhikkhus, it is not fitting for you, sons of good family who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith, that you should engage in such talk as this.”
“Bhikkhus, when you have gathered together, two things are to be practiced:
either a discourse on the Dhamma or noble silence.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
Living by no craft, desiring little,
with senses restrained and liberated in every way,
wandering without a home, without "mine-ness," and free from longing—
“Having abandoned conceit, he wanders alone as a bhikkhu.
Thus ends the ninth [verse].
